thread:
maya: quick q — we have a customer request to scrub all traces and cached payloads for acct `acme-inc`. Is there an approved one-off purge flow we should follow? need to know: who approves, audit log requirements, and whether we need to redact tokens before deleting or just delete.
neal: short answer: approvals from Legal + Security, infra run + audit. long answer below.
maya: ok, who exactly in Security? and infra run = you or ops?
neal: security: @olivia should sign off on scope. infra run = ops/infra team (dave usually coordinates one-offs) or we can run a pre-approved script if retained in runbook.
olivia: I can review — need the exact dataset list and retention tags. Do you have the S3 prefixes + trace index ids? also confirm if this includes cached KV cache entries in redis clusters.
maya: putting list here:
```
- s3://redwood-prod-traces/acme-inc/*
- redis://cache/tenant:acme-inc:*
- es-index traces-acme-2023-*
```
also there are some snapshot blobs in `backups/traces/acme-inc/` from nightly exports.
sam: reminder: before any deletion, we need an audit snapshot exported to a legal-hold bucket with restricted ACL and a signed retention waiver from customer if they requested deletion (for compliance).
security-bot: checklist: 1) Confirm requestor identity 2) Legal approval 3) Scoped dataset list 4) Pre-delete export (encrypted) 5) Deletion plan + rollback dry-run 6) Post-delete verification 7) Update audit log entry. :white_check_mark:
maya: requestor is support@acme-inc (they filed a GDPR Erasure request). Support has ticket #12345. I'll attach PII redaction checklist.
neal: about redaction vs delete: if data contains tokens/keys that could be re-issued, best practice is to rotate/expire those tokens and then delete traces. Redacting in-place is messy and could leave artifacts — prefer delete + record. For logs that must be retained for product telemetry, we can redact fields and retain aggregated metrics, but for customer erasure, delete customer-specific logs.
dave: infra can run `purge-tenant` job but it requires a signed one-off approval in the ops-runbook. Example command (dry-run):
```
./purge-tenant --tenant acme-inc --targets s3,redis,es --dry-run
```
then actual:
```
./purge-tenant --tenant acme-inc --targets s3,redis,es --confirm <approval-id>
```
maya: who provides approval-id? is that from Legal or Security?
olivia: approval-id is generated by Security after review. I'll need: requestor email, ticket link, dataset list, and confirmation that customer asked for deletion. After I review, I'll create approval artifact and add it to the ops-runbook entry.
sam: Legal needs to confirm no outstanding legal hold. I can ping legal, but need the ticket + env timestamps.
maya: adding ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-12345
infra-bot: scheduled maintenance windows for deletion: prefer off-peak (00:00-04:00 UTC). Any long-running deletes should have rate limits to avoid S3 request spikes.
dave: noted. infra will do dry-run Saturday 02:30 UTC, then actual after approvals. I'll post run logs to the ops channel and S3 audit bucket.
neal: one more: for traces stored in TTL'd systems (our kafka/redis ephemeral caches), confirm TTL doesn't resurrect anything — ensure we also clear any backup snapshots.
maya: snapshot cleanup: do we need manual removal from backups/traces/acme-inc/?
sam: yes, backups are separate. Ops should remove snapshots after Legal signs off. Make sure we capture a final audit export before removing backups.
olivia: I will review now. If all good, I'll produce approval-id within 24h. For emergency expedited erasure, escalate to me + legal and include the dataflow diagram.
maya: thanks — I'll assemble the dataset list and attach to ticket. tagging folks: @neal @dave @sam @olivia
neal: acked. I'll help run dry-run and verify checksums.
maya: thanks team :slightly_smiling_face:
